impact.text: ETH sent to Core is stuck forever.

precondition_sources.text: The pool is initialized at tick 0 with liquidity.
The victim submits a swap with a sqrtRatioLimit set near the current price for slippage protection, sending 10 ether via msg.value.

intent_sources.text: When a swap is executed with msg.value > 0, the native ETH debt accounting (_updatePairDebtWithNative) must be performed so the sent ETH is accounted for in the debt system.
A swap that would be a no-op (sqrtRatio == sqrtRatioLimit) with msg.value > 0 must revert rather than silently accept the ETH.
ETH sent to Core must not become permanently stuck; there must be a mechanism to account for or recover it.

impact.text: Attackers can front-run victim transactions to manipulate the pool price to exactly match the victim's `sqrtRatioLimit`, guaranteeing the exploit succeeds.

precondition_sources.text: The victim submits a swap with a sqrtRatioLimit set near the current price for slippage protection, sending 10 ether via msg.value.
An attacker monitoring the mempool can observe the victim's sqrtRatioLimit and front-run to move the price to exactly that limit.
